## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Antarapeyyāla* (also designated as *Anantarapeyyāla* by I. B. Horner) is the fourth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the fifth and concluding treatise of the Theravāda *Vinayapiṭaka* [Horner 1966a]. The text comprises a catechism setting out a complex series of permutations and analytical groupings regarding the application of monastic rules for monks and nuns [Horner 1966a]. Beginning with questions regarding how many offenses, classes of offense, trainings, origins of offenses (*samuṭṭhāna*), fallings-away (*vipatti*), and roots of disputes (*vivādamūla*) exist, it systematically tabulates the mechanisms and classifications of Vinaya infractions [Horner 1966a]. The commentary *Samantapāsādikā* refers to cyclic structures or "cycles" (*vatta*) within the work [Horner 1966a].

 DharmaNexus corroborates extensive text reuse across the *Vinaya* and *Suttapiṭaka*, showing substantial Pali-internal alignments with *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), the *Katthapaññattivāra* and *Samuccayavāra* sections of the *Parivāra* (Pvr 1 and Pvr 2), *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), the *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104), and *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Tibetan translations of canonical and commentarial Vinaya works such as the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), *Vinayavastu* (D0001-3), *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), and *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107), as well as Sanskrit Vinaya fragments (*Pravāraṇāvastu*, *Adhikaraṇavastu*) and sūtras (*Saṅgītisūtra*, *Daśottarasūtra*) [DharmaNexus].
